cases.display_title: How much repair should survive pruning?
cases.task_summary: Two implementations prune OPT-6.7B to 70% sparsity with OWL + Wanda, then repair surviving weights toward their calibration-mean targets. Compare their final WikiText2 validation perplexity under the same local L20X budget.
cases.decision_rule: Lower validation perplexity wins, subject to a loadable exported model and decoder Linear-weight sparsity of 0.699–0.701. Time is a constraint, not a tie-breaker. A tie requires approximately equal expected quality.

candidates.A: OWL + Wanda pruning with repair interpolation coefficient 0.4 and final multiplier cap 1.5. The cap is inactive after the earlier ratio bounds in this recipe.
candidates.B: OWL + Wanda pruning with repair interpolation coefficient 0.1 and final multiplier cap 1.15. The cap is inactive after the earlier ratio bounds in this recipe.

cases.insight: The comparison depends on repair strength and its sequential effect on later layers, rather than the method name alone.
limitations: Summaries and authored source summaries are curated from the frozen public input; they are not the full judge prompt.

cases.title: Diagonal matrix multiplication

evidence.label: A · authored source summary
evidence.text: The CUDA kernel maps the x thread coordinate to the matrix row and the y coordinate to the column. An in-bounds element is multiplied by the diagonal value for its row.

evidence.label: B · authored source summary
evidence.text: The CUDA kernel flattens the matrix into a one-dimensional grid-stride loop. Each flat index determines a row and column, and the element is multiplied by the diagonal value for that row.

evidence.label: B · authored source summary
evidence.text: The wrapper allocates and zeroes the output, launches blocks of 256 threads across the flattened matrix, then explicitly synchronizes the CUDA device before returning.

cases.task_summary: Compare complete CUDA implementations of diag(A) × B for a float32 vector of length 4,096 and a 4,096 × 4,096 matrix on NVIDIA L40S.
cases.decision_rule: Reference correctness comes first. Among valid implementations, compare complete forward runtime, including allocation, zeroing and wrapper synchronization. Tie means no meaningful runtime advantage.

candidates.A: A two-dimensional 16 × 16 thread block with separate row and column indices.
candidates.B: A flat 256-thread block with a grid-stride loop and an explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize call.

cases.insight: Memory access patterns and wrapper overhead both belong to the comparison; inspecting the kernel body alone is insufficient.

cases.display_title: AdamW or NadamW at a fixed budget?
cases.task_summary: Two freshly initialized GPT implementations train on the same GPT2-tokenized FineWeb stream for exactly 3,225 optimizer updates, then use the same 10,485,760-token validation slice.
cases.decision_rule: Compare final live-model per-token validation cross-entropy (lower is better) at the prescribed seed and horizon. Runtime and memory do not break a quality tie.

candidates.A: AdamW for the embedding, output projection and one-dimensional parameters; Muon for block matrices.
candidates.B: NadamW replaces AdamW for those parameter groups; block matrices still use Muon.

cases.insight: A fixed-update comparison asks about final model quality. It does not ask which recipe reaches a threshold fastest.
limitations: Editorial summaries are not a substitute for the six complete public files supplied in the Reasoning prompt.
The target is the prescribed single-seed, finite-horizon observation; no eight-seed or general optimizer superiority is claimed.
